symptom: Research-only synthetic Node 22.16.0 audit found that the shadow-evidence validator relied on mutable Set.prototype.has for allowed-field admission and on Set.prototype[Symbol.iterator] for required-field admission. A selective Set.has hook could admit unapproved top-level metadata; an empty Set iterator could skip a missing required privacy field after the evidence was re-digested. No production data or actual source evidence was involved.
lesson: A reusable Set-admission guardrail must also cover sanitized shadow-evidence validation. Fixed-schema required-field loops and unknown-field membership checks are both part of the fail-closed evidence boundary, even when a content digest is valid.
guardrail: Use module-owned indexed literal allowlists and index-based required-field loops, including forbidden metadata checks and verdict membership, rather than mutable Set.has or Set iteration. Regression-test selective unknown-field Set.has forgery and empty Set iterator missing-privacy-field admission; retain canonical digest and production isolation.
